slides.title: Brief Introduction 01 – Tester Data Tester Data are diagnostic command used to: • Check internal sw status and sensors •
slides.body:
All rights reserved.
- Check actuators status
- Allow components learning (pedals, valves,...)
Internal SW Status, sensors reading etc, can be known in two ways:
- By Local Identifier – It is an ID defined during development phase. This is the most common approach
used in ECUs in Stellantis programs and defines IDs for DIDs, IO Controls and Routine Controls;
- By Memory Address – It is an internal address where information to be read is stored.
In any case, many aspects such as conversion formulas, possibility to write by an external tool, data
protection by security access, etc. are defined. All those definitions are developed in order to allow the
vehicle to be serviced at the Plant (EOL) and in Aftersales and for development, fleet and validation
activities.

slides.title: What are DIDs? (1/2) 01 – Tester Data DID acronym stands for Diagnostic ID and identifies all engineering parameters gen
slides.body:
All rights reserved.
DID acronym stands for Diagnostic ID and identifies all engineering parameters generated by the sensors and
processed by the electronic system as well as some parameters calculated and used for control and implementation
that must be available on the diagnostic link.
These parameters will be made available on the diagnostic link, upon proper request, individually or in a group (with a
specific command); in addition, they must be accessible in the key ON status, with the motor running and at any vehicle
speed.
In case of errors on a certain component, the related parameter that is transmitted must be the one actually read by the
sensor and not the recovery parameter used by the electronic system.
If one or more parameters are not present in an application (version, outfitting), upon request by the instrument of that
specific parameter, the ECU shall respond with a negative response whose significance is “parameter not available”
(Nack 0x31).
DIDs can be divided into two categories:
- Readable DIDs - In that case, DID can be also indicated with acronym RDI, which stands for Readable Diagnostic
Identifier.
- Writeable DIDs - In that case, DID can be also indicated with acronym WDI, which stands for Writeable Diagnostic
Identifier.
- Both Readable and Writeable DIDs.

slides.title: Conversion Formulas 01 – Tester Data DIDs, IOs and routines give informations about values of interest related to compon
slides.body:
All rights reserved.
DIDs, IOs and routines give informations about values of interest related to components linked to the ECU through
CAN, LIN or hardwired and to learnings done.
Each diagnostic requirement has its own conversion formula to convert raw values in readable ones. There are
different types of conversion formulas:
- Linear conversion, used to convert raw values in physical ones as following:
y(x) = m(x) + b
where m(x) is the conversion factor and b is the offset. For each linear conversion, maximum and minimum
values, both HEX and DEC, shall be specified, adding unit of measurement also;
- Table conversion, where each state assumed by the signal takes on a HEX value as in the example below:
A mask specifies the maximum representable value based on the signal bit/byte size;
- Identical conversion, that is generally used to represent HEX or ASCII values as output.
Each conversion formula has its own ID, description and size.

slides.title: Brief Introduction 02 – Service $22/$2E Diagnostic Service $22 allows reading the engineering parameter. In that case, D
slides.body:
All rights reserved.
Diagnostic Service $22 allows reading the engineering parameter. In that case, DID can be also indicated with
acronym RDI, which stands for Readable Diagnostic Identifier. As per UDS protocol, a DID can be read using following
command:
$22 $XX XX
where $XX XX is RDI identifier, generally implemented in 2 bytes size. Positive response given by the ECU is:
$62 $XX XX $YY
where $XX XX is always the RDI identifier and $YY is the value you want to read.
Diagnostic Service $2E allows writing values in the engineering parameter. In that case, DID can be also indicated
with acronym WDI, which stands for Writeable Diagnostic Identifier. As per UDS protocol, a DID can be read using
following command:
$2E $XX XX $ZZ
where $XX XX is WDI identifier, generally implemented in 2 bytes size and $ZZ is the value you want to write. Positive
response given by the ECU is:
$6E $XX XX
where $XX XX is always the WDI identifier.

slides.title: How to test RDIs? 04 – RDI Testing RDI Testing is the most simple test to realize and it’s available in default session
slides.body:
All rights reserved.
RDI Testing is the most simple test to realize and it’s available in default session $10 01.
Below and example of a Test sequence:
TEST OK TEST NOT OK
$22 $XX $XX $22 $XX $XX
$62 $XX $XX $YY $7F $22 $11
Where:
- $XX XX is RDI ID;
- $YY is the HEX value read by the identifier. Reason of Negative Response
(e.g. Service Not Supported)

slides.title: Comparison with Internal Variable 04 – RDI Testing Is only one reading enough to say the test is OK? NO! At least 3 read
slides.body:
All rights reserved.
OK?
NO!
At least 3 readings are needed to say the test is OK and RDI is not blocked!
MAIN STEPS:
- Reading the RDI to know it’s current value;
- Put the internal SW variable to the minimum value in the range and read the RDI to check if the modified value is
readable;
- Put the internal SW variable to the maximum value in the range and read the RDI to check if the modified value is
readable.
